title: Unit – 5 : Session – 4 | Humanistic Education and Humane Society
sections: Q1. RIGHT UNDERSTANDING → VISUALISING THE COMPREHENSIVE HUMAN GOAL: with right understanding I can SEE the goal concretely: every self with right understanding and right feeling (happiness); every family prosperous — needs assessed, more produced than required, a feeling of sharing; society fearless — trust as the foundation, justice assured; nature in co-existence — protected and enriched. This visualisation is not utopian fantasy but the extrapolation of verified proposals: since harmony is inherent and natural acceptance is universal, the goal is achievable and the roadmap runs through education-sanskar, conduct, constitution and order.

Q2. THE HUMANISTIC TRADITION CYCLE and EDUCATION AS THE ENTRY POINT: humanistic education produces human beings with right understanding → such people live definite human conduct → they form humane families → humane families constitute a humane society and order → that order in turn provides humanistic education to the next generation — a self-sustaining cycle. The ENTRY POINT into this cycle, wherever it is broken, is EDUCATION-SANSKAR: because human inheritance is sanskar, not biology, transforming education transforms the next generation's conduct regardless of the present state — hence 'humanistic education' is the single leverage point from which the whole tradition can be regenerated.

Q3. HUMANE SOCIETY = PEOPLE-FRIENDLY + ECO-FRIENDLY: PEOPLE-FRIENDLY means every system — education, health, production, justice, exchange — is designed for mutual fulfilment of all human beings: no exploitation, no discrimination, trust as the social foundation, and assurance of the human goal for every family. ECO-FRIENDLY means the same systems operate in mutual enrichment with nature: cyclical production, right utilisation, protection and enrichment of the material, pranic and animal orders. The two are inseparable: a society that exploits nature ultimately exploits its own people (resource conflicts, displaced communities), and one that exploits people inevitably plunders nature.

Q4. ONE FEATURE I would make more humanistic — in EDUCATION: replace rank-based competition in classrooms with collaborative, excellence-based learning — group study where the stronger student guides the weaker (guidance as a value), assessment that measures understanding and participation rather than relative position. In MY PROFESSION-TO-BE (software): make the design review include an explicit 'mutual fulfilment check' — does this feature respect the user's Self (no dark patterns, no addiction loops) and nature (energy efficiency)? Both changes are small, implementable, and directly express right understanding in the system.
